study_identification_part.si_3_author_journal_year: Wolfers et al., Human Brain Mapping, 2021
study_identification_part.si_4_title: Replicating extensive brain structural heterogeneity in individuals with schizophrenia and bipolar disorder

nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: The study used Gaussian Process Regression (GPR) to predict VBM-based regional gray matter volumes from age and sex. The normative model was estimated using GPR in healthy individuals under 10-fold cross-validation, then applied to patients with schizophrenia and bipolar disorder. GPR provides both point estimates and measures of predictive confidence, allowing for the calculation of Z-scores reflecting deviations from the normative model.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: As in our previous article, we estimated the normative model using Gaussian Process Regression (GPR) to predict VBM based regional gray matter volumes across the brain from age and sex.

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: The study modeled voxel-based morphometry (VBM) data representing regional gray matter volumes. T1-weighted MRI images were processed using CAT12/SPM12 to obtain gray matter segments, which were smoothed with an 8mm FWHM Gaussian kernel prior to normative modeling.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: we estimated the normative model using Gaussian Process Regression (GPR) to predict VBM based regional gray matter volumes across the brain from age and sex

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: The normative model used age and sex as predictors to estimate the expected gray matter volume at each voxel. The model accounts for age-related changes in brain structure and sex differences.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: we estimated the normative model using Gaussian Process Regression (GPR) to predict VBM based regional gray matter volumes across the brain from age and sex
